title: After Getting Angry
description:
The day you got angry at Jiyeon.
You realized the words had gone too far once you got home.
Today a short text from Jiyeon.
'I've been thinking.'

choices.result_text:
'I went too far that day. I'm sorry.'
Jiyeon was quiet for a moment. '...I wasn't without fault either.'
The one who got angry going first. Hard — but the right direction.

'What did you think about?' you asked.
Jiyeon said 'I think we need to talk honestly.'
The anger became the start of a conversation.

title: The Seat She Left First
description:
The day Jiyeon stood up and left first.
Two months have passed.
A mutual contact mentioned she's been doing well.

choices.result_text:
'Heard you're doing well. You should have checked in.'
Jiyeon said 'you didn't have much room back then either.'
The person who leaves first isn't always in the wrong.

choices.text: Leave it. Good that she's well.
choices.result_text:
Good that she was well.
Maybe they'd just gone different directions.
That's also a kind of ending.

title: What Changed After Calling Her Out
description:
A month since you confronted Jiyeon directly.
Her manner has shifted slightly since.
Today Jiyeon brought up something serious first.

choices.result_text:
Jiyeon acknowledged a mistake she'd made.
She also said 'You did well saying that.'
Saying what needs to be said — wasn't ending things. It was moving them forward.

'It was nothing.'
Jiyeon said '...No — it was something.'
That stayed longer than expected.

title: The Weight of Honesty
description:
Two months since you opened up to Jiyeon.
Today she said:
"Oppa — what you told me then. I've been sitting with it."

choices.result_text:
Jiyeon said 'There's something I want to tell you too.'
Honesty called honesty back.
That conversation lasted another hour.

'You can forget it.'
Jiyeon said '...That's not something to forget.'
What you say honestly — others remember.

title: What Came After
description:
A month since you had a first meal alone with Daeun.
Today a KakaoTalk from Daeun.
'Minjun. Are you free next week?'

choices.result_text:
Daeun sent a place.
It was easier than the first time.
The second meeting — you could see it was her way of confirming what kind of person the first one was.

choices.text: "Been a bit busy lately. Let's do it next time."
choices.result_text:
Daeun said 'Sure, whenever.'
A second chance materialized.
Using it or not — that was your call.

title: After the Refusal
description:
Two months since you turned down Daeun's invitation.
Today you ran into her unexpectedly.
She smiled and said hello first.

choices.result_text:
Daeun said 'It's okay. It wasn't the right time.'
That came out warmer than expected.
A good person doesn't make a refusal into a wound.

'Hello.' That was all.
Daeun passed naturally too.
The refusal hadn't severed anything.

title: What Daeun Remembered
description:
It's been a while since you first spoke up when Daeun seemed to be having a hard time.
Over a meal today, Daeun said:
"Minjun — when you said something back then — do you remember that?"

choices.text: "I remember. You looked like you were really struggling."
choices.result_text:
Daeun said 'I was. That's what got me through it.'
The table went quiet for a moment.
A small kindness stays that long — you didn't know.

choices.text: "Did I? It's a bit fuzzy for me."
choices.result_text:
Daeun smiled. 'I remember.'
The things you do — get remembered somewhere you don't know.

title: The Text You Sent First
description:
A month since you worked up the nerve to text first.
Daeun had sent a short reply.
Today Daeun reached out first.
This time it was her.

choices.result_text:
You replied immediately.
Talked for a long time that evening.
The text you sent first — made this conversation.
The one who goes first gets there first.

You replied an hour later.
Daeun asked 'Were you busy?'
'No, just.' you said.
You'd made her wait for no reason.

title: After Running There
description:
The day you rushed there after hearing the news.
Your father was better than expected.
On the way home — the fact that you'd rushed felt slightly odd.

choices.result_text:
You put the next visit on the calendar.
It wasn't odd.
That was the natural thing.
Going when you feel like you should go.

It was a burden.
But you should go sometimes.
The memory of that run — made the next visit a little easier.

title: The Day You Skipped the Hospital
description:
Three months since you skipped accompanying your father to the hospital — too busy.
Today a call from your aunt.
'Minjun. Your father was really hurt that day.'

choices.result_text:
'Dad, I'm sorry I couldn't make it that day.'
Dad said 'It's fine, you were busy.'
You knew that 'it's fine' didn't mean fine.
Next time — you go.

You decided to go next time.
Your aunt's words kept nagging at you.
'He was really hurt.' That was his words spoken through her.

title: Coming Back from the Hospital
description:
After accompanying your father to his appointment.
What the doctor said in the consultation room kept echoing.
'No major issues for now — but please keep up the regular check-ups.'

choices.result_text:
You booked it for three months out.
Dad said 'What for —' but he seemed pleased.
Taking care of it came before taking him.

choices.text: Tell him to go on his own
choices.result_text:
'Dad, you really have to go to the next one.'
Dad said 'I know.'
Whether he'd actually go — unknown.
In the end it was going to have to be together.

title: The Morning After the Promotion
description:
The promotion came through.
The team lead shook your hand yesterday.
This morning the desk is the same — but something felt different.
So this is what responsibility weighs.

choices.result_text:
You said 'Thanks for the support' to each one.
They all smiled.
The promotion was a signal to do better in front of these people.

You didn't act different.
Because nothing was different.
But the team saw it differently — you found that out later.

title: When the Certificate Comes Up
description:
The certification you earned.
One line on the resume — but today in the interview they focused heavily on it.
Dug deeper than expected.

choices.result_text:
Thirty minutes on just that topic.
The interviewer said 'You seem to enjoy this field.'
A certification isn't passed — it's known.
Knowing it when you got it was right.

You said it straight.
The interviewer said 'That's refreshingly honest.'
Not overstating. That was evaluated too.

title: The Headhunting Call
description:
A headhunter called.
"It's over 30% above your current package.
If you're open to a move, would you be interested in a meeting?"

choices.result_text:
You met.
The package was good.
A move decision isn't just about numbers — but having options was an asset in itself.

'I don't think it's the right time. Thank you.'
The headhunter said 'I'll keep your contact.'
Not now — doesn't mean not ever.

title: The Day It's Paid Off
description:
Today you made the final payment on the debt from the MLM.
You opened the banking app — loan balance: 0 won.
You stared at the screen for a long time.

choices.result_text:
You wrote the date.
'It's done today.'
No name of who you borrowed from. No reason.
Just — done.

You quietly closed the app.
Nothing to say particularly.
Just lighter.

title: The Day After the Holiday
description:
You held on and got through the holiday.
All the questions. All the comparisons. All passed.
This morning — tired, but somehow lighter.

choices.result_text:
You decided something would be different at the next one.
A different answer. A different way of talking.
Surviving the same way every year — that's not surviving. It's burning out.

It passed.
It will pass again.
For now, that's everything.
